The original proposal addresses enzyme selection under industrial wastewater conditions.
The current research focuses on PET degradation assays with recorded TPA concentrations.
Temperature, pH and reaction duration describe the available assay environment.
Dyes, PU, phenolics and other waste streams remain expansion targets.
Build a traceable dataset linking protein sequences, assay conditions and measured TPA.
Compare environmental features with frozen ESM-2 protein representations.
Evaluate generalization to held-out proteins using grouped cross-validation.
Support a recommendation prototype and identify the evidence needed for future optimization.
The confirmed research experiment does not validate the separately served legacy model.

EnzAIme tests a specific application of these ideas. It does not claim to solve every gap.
Protein representation + environmental conditions + recorded activity + retained provenance
Can protein sequence representations and environmental conditions jointly support reliable enzyme activity prediction under plastic-degradation conditions?
The current experiments test this question under limited protein coverage.
Confirmed labels trace to PAZy assay records. Other sources do not imply complete label coverage.
Labels derive from recorded experimental measurements, including digitized source values. Duration is normalized to hours.
Target field: target_value_standardized. Concentration is an assay endpoint, not a universal fitness score.
Repeated conditions and duplicate patterns were audited. They were not automatically discarded.
47 of 48 repeated-condition groups have different targets. All 48 have recorded metadata differences.
Matching protein, pH, temperature and duration does not establish identical experimental protocols.
Protein ID is for grouping. Source IDs, outcomes and protocol-rich metadata are excluded.
Salinity, COD, BOD and pollutant type lack confirmed-label coverage. EC numbers are empty in this cohort.
Material descriptions are source/protocol-specific. Substrate is PET in all 221 rows, so it adds no variation.
25/25 confirmed proteins have finite vectors. Current pooling includes special tokens.

title: What the current results tell us

text: What the current results tell us
Environment-only shows positive mean ranking signal (Spearman 0.313).
ESM-2 alone generalizes poorly in this small dataset. Adding conditions helps relative to ESM-2 alone.
Negative mean R² and large fold differences limit claims about absolute prediction.
These findings concern this dataset and setup. They do not establish that protein language models are ineffective.
Research experiment output: saved out-of-fold prediction plots.
Per-fold and per-protein diagnostics are complete. Interpretation and model refinement continue.
Observed TPA reaches 47,000 µM. The fold’s training targets reach only about 6,860 µM. The retained provenance supports 47 mM converted to µM.
Overprediction for this protein contributes 99.3% of B’s and 98.0% of C’s fold-3 squared error.
Large values and repeated conditions require source review, not automatic removal.

These are exploratory follow-ups. Final model selection and an independently validated serving artifact remain open.

Sources: Project brief updated against existing reports
Open-source tools and reused embeddings support feasibility. Environmental benefit requires experimental and deployment evidence.
EnzAIme establishes a provenance-aware framework for condition-aware enzyme research.
The current work provides confirmed PET/TPA labels, frozen ESM-2 features and protein-grouped evaluation.
Controlled ablation shows environmental ranking signal alongside substantial prediction and generalization limits.
Further data, model refinement and experimental validation are necessary before industrial use.
